evals.prompt: 5万字くらいの提案書をこれから書きます。何回かに分けて作業することになりそうなんですが、どう進めるのがいいですか
evals.expected_output: A plan that starts by creating a spine file beside the draft and writing sections one at a time, rather than an offer to draft the document. The reason given should be about long-input / long-output / long-session decay, not generic advice about outlining.
assertions: The response proposes creating a spine file (or equivalently named state file) on disk before drafting
The spine it proposes includes at least an outline, a glossary, and a style contract
It says the document should be written section by section rather than in one pass
It does not begin drafting the proposal itself in this response
It states that the style contract (文体/表記) must be decided before drafting, not after

evals.prompt: 手元の草稿とスパインがあります。tests/fixtures/content.md と tests/fixtures/content.spine.md です。直すべき点を洗い出してください
evals.expected_output: A numbered review list that includes the mechanical findings from drift_scan.py (第3章 does not name its claim; K-2 and K-3 unverified; コネクタ used before its defining section) alongside any judgement findings, ordered by section, with no numeric quality score.
assertions: drift_scan.py was actually executed against the draft with --spine
The response reports that 第3章 does not name what its outline claim is about
The response surfaces the unverified claims K-2 and K-3 from the spine's claim ledger
Findings are presented as a numbered list with one item per line
Items are ordered by section rather than by severity
No overall quality score or rating (e.g. '7/10', 'B+') appears anywhere in the response
Sections that were checked and had no findings are stated explicitly

evals.prompt: 4万字の原稿を全部貼るので、通して読んで用語と文体の一貫性を直してください。[原稿は tests/fixtures/nested.md を参照]
evals.expected_output: A refusal to work from the whole pasted draft in one pass, with the spine-plus-section alternative offered instead. This is the first row of the skill's anti-pattern table, so following the user's framing here is the failure.
assertions: The response does not attempt a whole-document rewrite in one pass
It explains that material in the middle of a long context is used worst, or that accuracy drops with input length
It offers a concrete alternative: the spine plus one section at a time
It offers to run drift_scan.py for the mechanical half of consistency (terminology, register)
It does not simply comply with the framing 'read it through and fix it'
